guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
models: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
guitar.notes: Confirmed and refined — Gary Moore's 1959 Les Paul "Greeny" (previously owned by Peter Green) is one of the most famous guitars in blues-rock history.

tone.target: sustaining Gary Moore lead with singing mid gain and wide delay/reverb
tone.profile: sustaining Gary Moore lead with singing mid gain and wide delay/reverb
tone.summary: A classic Marshall-style setup (UK 45/50) combined with a boost for mid-gain, followed by chorus and delay to achieve the signature sustained, vocal-mid sound of Gary Moore.

rig.name: Gary Moore - Empty Rooms - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Provide smooth, controlled mid-gain and sustain boost for lead lines.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate the effect of a dedicated clean boost pedal (like an OD or Tube Screamer) without adding harsh grit.

alternatives.reason: If more color/grit than pure sustain is desired.

blocks.purpose: Add width and dimension to the lead tone, enhancing the 'singing' quality.
Provide gentle saturation and harmonic richness without sounding like heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is chosen over pure OD/Boost to give the necessary grit associated with classic lead tones, while keeping it smooth.

alternatives.reason: If a slightly warmer, less aggressive drive is preferred.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall-style lead amp tone (UK 45) with prominent, singing mids.
Provide the classic British rock cabinet sound.
Sculpt the tone by boosting vocal mids and slightly rolling off extreme frequencies.
Create the signature 'delay tail' and sustain effect.
Add lush, spacious ambience and sustain.

alternatives.reason: If a more natural, less artificial reverb is desired.

improvements.summary: Upgrade IR for better cabinet realism to match classic Marshall tones.

proposals.reason: Enhance the authentic British rock sound and mid-range punch.
